notes.title: Driver4VR Update 5.14.2.0 - JoyCon Gyro scale to support non-genuine models
notes.notes: In this release, I've added a Gyroscope Scale option for Joy-Cons. This allows you to adjust the sensitivity of the gyroscope, which can be particularly helpful if you're using non-genuine Joy-Cons that may have a different sensor calibration.

notes.title: Driver4VR Update 5.14.1.0 - Wii Remote now works with Sensor Bar
notes.notes:
Introducing support for Sensor Bar that works with Wii Remote when used as Virtual Tracker. Sensor Bar at the moment only provides drift correction. There is no positional tracking.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40597360/c0e3a76b29a7e4586213e381db75046ad6d54df3.png[/img]

notes.title: Driver4VR Update 5.14 - Wii Remote Update
notes.notes:
Hello,

This update for the Wii Remote adds support for more recent models of Wii Remote (e.g., RVL-CNT-01-TR). Until now, such devices were not easy to detect by Driver4VR, but this should now work without any issues.

Let me know in case of problems :)
Greg

notes.title: Driver4VR Update 5.13.0.0 - PSMoveService to PSMoveServiceEx Update
notes.notes:
Hello,

Since PSMoveService has not been updated for a while, Driver4VR has now been updated to use PSMoveServiceEx. This doesn't change much of the instructions; the main changes are related to the installation process. The UI is also very similar but has many great new features. PSMoveServiceEx is a great enhancement to PSMoveService, and I am thankful to the developer, Timocop, for that.

Here is a short info about the changes being made: [url=https://support.driver4vr.com/faq/psmoveserviceex-setup-and-updating-psmoveservice-to-psmoveserviceex/]Updating PSMoveService to PSMoveServiceEx[/url]..

In case of problems, please contact me via the [url=https://support.driver4vr.com/]support page[/url].

Enjoy :)

notes.title: Driver4VR Update 5.12.4 - Introducing Puppeteer (Kinetic DLC)
notes.notes:
Puppeteer is a new upgrade to full-body pose estimation! It lets you control your virtual character's full body moves using VR controllers, giving you more freedom to express yourself in the virtual world. 
Just move your hands with the controllers while holding the grip button, and your character follows suit, making your gaming experience more immersive and fun than ever before.

To enable/disable Puppeteer mode hold controllers above the head and hold grip for a while.

Now with Puppeteer mode when you hold grip, you start controlling your feet. That is all :) Check out the below video on how it works in action.

[previewyoutube=ECH0vVU-bDs;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Driver4VR Update 5.10.0.0 - Anaglyph 3D on Monitor or TV
notes.notes:
An anaglyph is a stereoscopic 3D image that combines two offset images, using red and cyan filters. When viewed through glasses with corresponding red and cyan lenses, each eye perceives a slightly different image, resulting in a three-dimensional effect.

After enabling tVR, you need to open settings, turn Anaglyph mode ON, and restart SteamVR. Don't forget to put your glasses on :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40597360/232da017051e8ed00c9bf2f33c0a7c493ad16486.png[/img]

notes.title: Driver4VR Beta Update - Body Tracking in VRChat on standalone Quest (Beta 1)
notes.notes:
Hello.
This is very first version of Body Tracking with Kinect for VRChat on standalone Oculus Quest 2. Currently it works only with Open Beta version that you can download from App Lab - https://www.oculus.com/experiences/quest/4821132827998004/ . There will be full tutorial video about that. I am providing instruction based on video script below.

For questions or issues join my Discord https://discord.gg/Bks9YyX in channel #osc-quest-body.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40597360/4aa7b9e9c71572640e71511e779aa6f5f161247a.png[/img]
	
You will need a PC but it doesn’t have to be VR Ready PC or even gaming PC.
Even a typical office laptop will do the job. Of course you need Kinect One or Kinect 360 and adapter that will connect your Kinect to the PC. For Kinect 360 you need USB 2.0 and for Kinect One you need USB 3.0. Also PC and Quest must be in same local network.
On your PC you need install Driver4VR from the Steam and Kinect Drivers. When you start Driver4VR  you will see two options and you need to select one for OSC-VRChat Also when first starting Driver4VR  it will attempt to register in SteamVR. This is only required for PC-VR setup and  you can ignore this message.
Now check IP address on your Quest. Go to Quick Settings, WI Fi, Your network, Advanced and here it is.
Enter IP address in Driver4VR and press Start. Click “Show preview” and check if your pose is detected.
Currently there is no way to check in Driver4VR if there is connection to VRChat on your Quest. But that might change with further VRChat updates.
Switch back to your Quest and VRChat. In Settings, “Tracking and IK” section there are only few settings until we send tracking data.
Now open Quick Menu, Options, OSC and make sure it is set to Enabled.
To double check connection open OSC Debug. You should see that the data is coming from Kinect and Driver4VR to your Quest and VRChat.
Right now, the trackers should appear in VRChat. We should see also more settings  in “Tracking and IK” section. Ensure that “Toggle FBT” is Enabled.
First change Skeleton scale in Driver4VR so the feet trackers are aligned with the floor when you are standing. Pay attention that you look forward. Not up or down but forward. You can double tap Quest 
for pass through view. Or take it off for a while.
Now stay directly in front of the Kinect and spread your feet parallel to the device. Next look directly to Kinect, that is very important. And click Auto Center OSC Trackers. If your feet are reversed then press the Auto Center button again.
Final step is to calibrate Avatar. If avatar’s feet are above or below floor then adjust avatar’s height. 
Finally just stay in T pose and press both triggers.
When starting next time around start Driver4VR and you should see trackers immediately in VRChat. Perform Auto Center OSC Trackers and Avatar T-pose calibration as usual.
That is all.
If you don’t see trackers, make sure that Quest IP address did not change. In most cases it should not. Check also if OSC is Enabled and data is coming in OSC Debug window. 
Thanks 😊

notes.title: Driver4VR 5.6.14.0 - Small update
notes.notes:
Driver4VR has been updated to version 5.6.14.0.

This build contains the following changes:
- Camera Markers crash when 2 PS Eyes are connected - fix
- Allow set 'no preview' during Kinect calibration to not take extra USB bandwidth that was causing freezing.
- Updated Wii library to better detect/reconnect to Remotes.

Best :)
Greg
